pages.title: Home
pages.purpose: Front page: announces the new AIO Platform, states what AIO does, and sends visitors to the main sections and the latest news.
pages.summary: The main heading is "All new AIO Platform is now available", with a button to the platform and a YouTube video from the Director, Julian Thomas. A section "The Digital Transformation Challenge" explains why researchers need access to platform data. Four cards follow (Digital Research Platform, Data Collection Tools, Data Governance and Management, Outreach and Training), then "Work with us", "Participate" and a partner statement (ARDC, NCRIS). A grid shows the 4 newest posts: "The all new AIO platform is here!" (2026-09-23), "SICSS-Melbourne 2026 – Our First Week" (2026-06-24), "Shaping the future at Building Digital Platform Observatories" (2026-06-24), "SICSS 2026 starts in Melbourne" (2026-06-20).
pages.verdictReason: This is the page that WordPress treats as the front page: its body class is "home" and its canonical link is "/". It was modified last (7 October 2026). Carry it over, but fold in the shorter wording of /home-2/ and cut the repeated sections.
externalLinks: Try it out here (AIO Platform) -> https://app.internetobservatory.org.au/
Latest News & Events / View all news + events -> https://internetobservatory.org.au/news-and-events/
media: YouTube video "What is AIO? Introducing the AIO Platform" -> https://youtu.be/15xDm12TMFU
problems: Two pages are titled "Home". The menu item "Home" goes to /home-2/, but the logo goes to this page (/).
The video is configured to start by itself with sound on and to repeat (settings in the HTML: autoplay true, mute false, loop true). I did not render the page, so I did not watch this happen.
The level-2 heading under "The Digital Transformation Challenge" is a full sentence of 32 words.
The card links use /observe and /learn. These work only through WordPress redirects.
The "View all news + events" button is in the HTML twice (one copy for desktop, one for mobile).
One news card shows two overlapping categories: "News" and "News and Events".
The text repeats itself: "The tools that power digital observation" restates the cards above it, and "Work with us" repeats the Get Started introduction word for word.
The page loads 26 stylesheet files and 19 script files, and its main content holds 28 image elements.

pages.title: Home
pages.purpose: A second, newer draft of the home page, which the main menu item "Home" opens.
pages.summary: The main heading is "Tools to observe and understand the digital world", with the subheading "Collect, manage and analyse digital platform data" and a "Get Started" button. Three links follow: Explore the Platform, Data Collection Tools, Participate / Donate Your Data. The rest repeats the front page: a shorter "Digital Transformation Challenge" text, the same four cards with slightly longer text, "Work with us", "Participate", the partner statement, and the same grid of the 4 newest posts. It has no platform announcement and no video.
pages.verdictReason: Merge into the new home page (/). About 70 per cent of the text is the same as on /. Its hero wording and its short challenge text are clearer than those on /, so use them there. Then drop this address and redirect it to /.
externalLinks: Participate / Donate Your Data -> /participate// (double slash, redirects to https://internetobservatory.org.au/participate/)
Read more about AIO and the challenge it solves -> https://internetobservatory.org.au/about/
problems: Duplicate home page. The address "home-2" is a WordPress default name, and the page is open to search engines with its own canonical link.
The four "What we want to achieve" cards are link elements with no target. A click on them goes nowhere.
The link "Participate / Donate Your Data" has a double slash (/participate//).
The label "Explore the Platform" opens the Explore page of the website, not the AIO Platform (app.internetobservatory.org.au).
This page has no link to the AIO Platform in its main content, although / leads with it.
The level-2 heading under "The Digital Transformation Challenge" is two sentences (41 words).
The "View all news + events" button is in the HTML twice (one copy for desktop, one for mobile).
The site search lists this page as "Home" next to the real home page.

pages.verdictReason: The text is short and useful, and it is the natural entry page for researchers. Add the missing links to each step when it moves to the new site.
problems: The main content has 0 links. The text names the Resources section, the About page, the Ethics section, an ethics template and the platform, but links to none of them.
Step 5 says to create a project on the platform, with no link or button to https://app.internetobservatory.org.au/.
The text mentions an "Ethics section". The menu has no item with that name.
"HREC" is not written out on this page.
The step icons repeat: one icon serves steps 2 and 4, another serves steps 3 and 5.
The page sits under /explore/ in the address, but the menu shows it before "Explore" at the same level.

pages.title: Contact Us
pages.purpose: Gives the contact email address, the social media accounts and an enquiry form.
pages.summary: The page gives the address contact@internetobservatory.org.au and three social links (Bluesky, YouTube, LinkedIn). An enquiry form has 4 required fields: Name, Email, Subject and Message, and a 'Submit Enquiry' button.

Its sections are Information Collection, Use and Disclosure of Information, Data Security, User Rights, Cookies and Website Tracking, and Policy Updates. It states that the site uses cookies and Google Analytics, and it ends with 'Effective date: 17 April, 2025'.

Site link in the text (uses http, not https) -> http://internetobservatory.org.au/
problems: The labels do not match the content. The URL is /terms/, the HTML <title> is 'Terms of Service', the H1 is 'Terms & Conditions' and the footer link is 'Terms'. The body calls itself 'this Privacy Policy' 4 times.
The site has no actual terms of service text.
The HTML has 6 empty H4 headings, one before each of the 6 section headings.
The effective date is 17 April 2025, but the page metadata shows a last change on 30 April 2026.

pages.title: Algorithms dictate everything we see. Time to crack them
pages.author: Daniel Angus (the WordPress account that posted the item, shown as 'By Daniel Angus'; the text has no byline)
pages.purpose: A short news item that points readers to a podcast episode in which Daniel Angus talks about AIO.
pages.summary: The item says that social media algorithms shape what people see and that Meta and Google keep the details secret. It says researchers in the Australian Internet Observatory partnership are working to change that. Daniel Angus of QUT joins Bension Siebert on The Briefing podcast. A Spotify player for the episode follows the text.
problems: Very thin: 114 words of main text.
The only text link goes to the podcast show, not to the episode. The episode is reachable only through the embedded player.
The item gives no episode date and does not name the podcast publisher.
The player is a third-party iframe from Spotify. It adds weight and tracking to a very short page.
The featured image has no alt text.
The byline is the name of the WordPress account, not a stated author.

pages.title: Research Ethics Guide
pages.author: Jigya Khabar (the WordPress account that posted the item, shown as 'By Jigya Khabar'; the text has no byline)
pages.purpose: A long guide for researchers on the ethics of research with digital media data, with sample wording for an ethics application.
pages.summary: The guide explains the four principles of the National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research and applies each to digital media research. It covers citizen science, the FAIR and CARE data principles, the Human Research Ethics Committee process, and data retention, destruction and security. It gives four sample paragraphs for an ethics application (data collection, data security, third-party data, de-identification). It ends with one section on informed consent in data donation.
media: Featured image (decorative pattern, no alt text) -> https://internetobservatory.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Pattern_15.jpg
problems: The page has zero links. It names the National Statement, the Australian Code, the FAIR and CARE principles and AIO tools, and links to none of them.
It has four in-text citations (Strycharz et al., 2024; van Driel et al., 2022; Ohme et al., 2021; ACSA, 2025) and no reference list.

It cites the National Statement as '2007, updated 2018'. A web search summary says the 2025 edition has been in effect since 23 June 2026 and replaced the 2023 edition. I could not confirm this on the NHMRC page itself, because the request timed out. Another post on the site (Building global connections) already cites the 2025 edition.
Very long for one page: 2,158 words, with no contents list and no anchors.
Only 7 real headings (H2). 11 sub-headings are bold paragraphs and 4 are italic paragraphs, so they are not headings for a screen reader or for a contents list.

The page ends after one consent section, 'Data Donation: Full Informed Consent'. The section compares data donation with other methods, but no other method follows. I checked that the live page and the JSON copy end at the same sentence, so the guide looks unfinished.
Three tool names appear without a definition or a link: Data Donation Registration System (DDRS), AIO Data Laboratory and Data Relay.
The sample paragraphs contain placeholders in square brackets, such as [Platform Name]. These are intended, but they need care in Markdown.
The guide is stored as a blog post with a date and a personal byline, not as a maintained page.
pages.verdictReason: It is original AIO guidance and one of the two items in the Guide category. Carry it as a guide page with a contents list, real headings, links and a reference list. An owner must update the National Statement reference and decide whether the missing consent sections exist.

pages.title: FAQ

pages.title: What political ads are Australians seeing online?
pages.author: Daniel Angus; Christine Parker; Giselle Newton; Kate Clark; Mark Andrejevic
pages.purpose: A republished article from The Conversation on political advertising seen online before the 2025 Australian federal election.
pages.summary: The authors tracked political ads on Facebook, Instagram and TikTok through a panel of Australians with an ad-tracking app, and through the PoliDashboard tool. They found about one third-party ad for each party ad and a rise in astroturfing, which means hiding the sponsor behind a grassroots-sounding name. They note that truth in political advertising is not required by federal law. Less than 2% of the ads that participants saw were political. They call for independent observation of online political communication.
externalLinks: 'Australian Internet Observatory' (link text; target is an ADM+S Ad Observatory page) -> https://www.admscentre.org.au/australian-ad-observatory-investigating-mobile-and-dynamic-advertising-via-computational-and-participatory-approaches/
problems: The content holds a second H1 heading (the subtitle 'Astroturfing, fake grassroots groups, and outright falsehoods'), so the page has two H1 headings.

Typo carried in the text: 'Acknowlegement'.

The featured image has no alt text.
pages.verdictReason: It is a substantial article by AIO researchers and is the fullest account of the election monitoring work. Carry it as a republished item with the five authors in the front matter, the subtitle as a subtitle field, and a canonical link to the original.

pages.title: Data Download Packages Explainer
pages.author: AIO
pages.purpose: Long reference text for researchers on Data Download Packages (DDPs): what they are, what they hold and how to use them in a study.
pages.summary: A DDP is the personal data archive that a user can request from a platform. The page explains the legal basis, and what the DDPs of Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, Google Takeout and ChatGPT contain. It lists what DDPs hold and what they lack, and the problems of unstable formats and language-dependent file names. It then gives the steps of data cleaning and advice for before, during and after a study. It names the AIO's "Data Relay" tool as the support for this work.

The page has no image, diagram or video of the method.

The page shows two category labels run together ("ExplainerResource").
